title: PH joins India-led coalition to boost disaster-resilient infrastructure
summary: MANILA, Philippines — The Philippines is turning to an India-led global coalition for technical expertise and possible financing to build infrastructure that can better withstand floods and other…

blocks.text: MANILA, Philippines — The Philippines is turning to an India-led global coalition for technical expertise and possible financing to build infrastructure that can better withstand floods and other disasters, according to Malacañang.
President Ferdinand R. Marcos Jr. on Saturday met with officials of the Coalition for Disaster Resilient Infrastructure (CDRI) in New Delhi as Manila formally joined the group as its 71st member.
Marcos is currently in India to attend the 18th Brics Summit as this year’s chair of the Association of the Southeast Asian Nations (Asean), at the invitation of Indian Prime Minister Narendra Modi.

The membership comes as the Marcos administration faces growing pressure to improve the country’s flood-control and other disaster mitigation infrastructure amid increasingly adverse weather events worsened by climate change.

Presidential Communications Office (PCO) Secretary Dave Gomez said the CDRI could help the Philippines learn from other countries how to design and build roads, bridges and ports that can withstand disasters and climate-related risks.
“First and foremost, they will teach us—this is essentially a sharing of experiences among coalition members on how to deal with disasters and how to build disaster resilience,” Gomez said.
The coalition could also help the Philippines access financing for projects meant to make infrastructure more resilient, he added.
According to Gomez, investing in stronger infrastructure before disasters strike would be more beneficial in the long run than spending heavily on reconstruction and recovery after calamities.

The Philippines has been dealing with recurring flooding, particularly in Metro Manila and other urban and low-lying areas, with the government pursuing large-scale flood-control and drainage projects while also reviewing existing infrastructure.

The CDRI membership provides the Philippines an opportunity to tap the experience of other countries in addressing such challenges, particularly in designing infrastructure that can withstand extreme weather and other hazards.
CDRI Director-General Amit Prothi welcomed the Philippines’ membership and said he looks forward to working with Philippine institutions on disaster-resilient infrastructure.
He cited the Philippines’ extensive experience and knowledge in dealing with flooding, earthquakes and volcanic activity.
Knowledge sharing

Prothi said the country’s long-standing efforts to address these challenges could provide valuable lessons for other countries, especially in its experience in disaster risk management, preparedness, response, and resilient recovery.

Launched by the Indian government in 2019, the CDRI is a voluntary and nonbinding global partnership that brings together governments, international organizations, financial institutions, private companies and academic institutions.
It seeks to promote the sharing of expertise and best practices, strengthen technical capabilities and encourage investments in infrastructure that can withstand disasters and climate change.

The coalition also focuses on shaping policies and financing, integrating risk-aware development, scaling up resilience actions, and building stakeholder capacity to protect vulnerable communities and high-risk regions.
$10 trillion global investment

By 2050, CDRI aims to drive $10 trillion in resilient infrastructure investments and services to improve environmental quality, livelihoods and well-being for more than three billion people worldwide.
Overall, the CDRI is composed of 71 members, including 59 countries and 12 partner organizations.
The Philippines is the second Southeast Asian country to join the coalition after Vietnam.
The Department of Public Works and Highways has been designated to represent the Philippines in the CDRI.

The country’s participation in CDRI also forms part of the Philippines-India Strategic Partnership and aligns with the Philippine Development Plan (PDP) 2023-2028, the National Adaptation Plan (NAP) 2023-2050, and the National Disaster Risk Reduction and Management Plan (NDRRMP) 2020-2030. /gsg
